transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start time: 08:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SRE), Sarah Miller (CTO, Nova), Jamal Reyes (Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (Security), Tom Wu (DevOps)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick roll call before we dive in.
[00:07] Sarah Miller: Yep, here. Jamal here, Tom, Lena on.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood here, Marco as well. I'll take the first bit on the network notes later.
[00:20] Alex Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: network status, bench results, tuning updates, security questions, next steps. If we miss something, flag it.
[00:30] Jamal Reyes: Quick note — we ran into a routing thing Friday, some traffic to S3 for model artifacts was hitting the NAT gateway and we spiked charges, so we tried a route to a VPC endpoint but it's not propagating across the peering.
[00:45] Marco Diaz: Right, we saw the same logs. Looks like the peering is active but the route table on the Redwood side wasn't pushing the specific prefix for the VPC endpoint — could be a cross-account propagation flag.
[00:58] Priya Nair: That aligns with what we saw in the pilot env. On our default config we expect customers to either use S3 VPC endpoints or to egress through a transit gateway; the peer route propagation sometimes needs the explicit allow.
[01:12] Tom Wu: We don't have transit gateway in this pilot, so we're trying to keep it simple with peering + endpoints. Any quick recommended ACLs or security group rules?
[01:25] Priya Nair: Keep the SGs narrow: control plane port 8443 from management CIDR, model-serving ports between the subnets. For egress, the S3 endpoint should be suffcient. We'll send exact SG examples after the call.
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: On compliance side, we need to verify the KMS flow — who holds the keys if we run in Private mode? Is Redwood managing KMS or we bring our own? Also audit log retention length?
[01:55] Alex Chen: Good Q. For Private we support customer-managed KMS; you can bring your key (BYOK) and integrate HSM if needed. Audit logs are configurable; default retention is 90 days for the pilot, enterprise can extend. We'll loop in security to do a deep-dive.
[02:10] Sarah Miller: Sounds good, please put the details in the security doc.
[02:15] Priya Nair: Moving to bench results — thanks for uploading last week's run. We re-ran with the runtime v2.1 kernel patches on our side and saw P95 token latency drop from ~420ms to ~310ms for the 2k context profile.
[02:31] Jamal Reyes: Yeah, we saw improvement after the quantization flags you suggested, but there was some instability at higher concurrency — the KV cache hit rate dropped.
[02:43] Marco Diaz: The concurrency instability maps to the batching config — when we increased max batch size to 32 we saw better throughput but some requests saw tail latency. We recommended dynamic batch sizing in the config, which can help smooth tails.
[02:59] Jamal Reyes: Do you think it's safe to push the quantization to int8 across all models? We worried about accuracy for our summarization workload.
[03:10] Priya Nair: For summarization we recommend mixed precision or per-model quant profiles. We can flag the model with conservative quant, and run evals against your prompt set. That way we keep quality within your SLA.
[03:22] Sarah Miller: Can we get an eval run against our 50 prompt goldset this week?
[03:27] Alex Chen: Yes — we'll coordinate. Priya, can you own that?
[03:30] Priya Nair: Yep, I'll run the eval. Need the goldset CSV in the shared folder.
[03:34] Tom Wu: Uploaded it earlier under /shared/pilot/goldset.csv — there may be a formatting quirk though, we had some stray commas.
[03:42] Priya Nair: I'll sanity-check it.
[03:45] [04:00] Alex Chen: Security deep-dive — Lena, what are the must-haves for you?
[04:05] Lena Ortiz: SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning, RBAC role separation for ops vs devs, BYOK KMS workflow, and tamper-evident audit logs. Also data residency — we need logs stored in eu-west-1 for this project.
[04:20] Priya Nair: We support SAML and SCIM, RBAC is configurable in the console, and BYOK is in our Private offering. For audit logs we can route to your CloudWatch/logging endpoint; we'll confirm retention and residency options.
[04:35] Jamal Reyes: One more network gotcha — our egress via the NAT is adding 30–40ms to p95 when loading model weights, is there a way to stage artifacts inside the Redwood subnet to avoid that?
[04:50] Marco Diaz: We can stage weights on a co-located storage mount or use a pre-warmed cache in the same AZ; that reduces initial cold-start fetches. We'll provide a diagram.
[05:05] Priya Nair: Also for cutover we recommend using prefix caching so the KV cache warms during a staged rollout. That should reduce cold token penalty.
[05:16] Sarah Miller: When you say pre-warmed cache, is that automatic or a manual step?
[05:20] Priya Nair: It's a config — we can script warmers that hit the model endpoints with your top prompts to populate cache before traffic shift. Redwood's Optimize tooling can generate suggested warmers.
[05:33] Alex Chen: Alright, planning: can we agree on a final pilot run week of 2026-04-06? Jamal, is that feasible?
[05:40] Jamal Reyes: Yes, should be ok, assuming we finish peering and the route propagation fixes this week.
[05:46] Lena Ortiz: Also lock in security deep-dive before the final run.
[05:50] Alex Chen: We'll do that, target the week of 2026-04-03 for security review.
[05:56] [06:10] Tom Wu: Small thing — can we get the exact kernel flags you changed for v2.1? Our infra likes exact reproducibility.
[06:18] Priya Nair: Sure, I'll paste the flag list — quant: enable-int8-mixed=false, attention-kernel=optimA_v3, batch-dynamic=true, kv-cache-size=auto, thread-pin=affinity. I'll include the full command and notes in the doc.
[06:34] Jamal Reyes: Thanks. Also any thoughts on fallback routing to hosted Redwood for spikes? We want to avoid failures but keep data in our VPC when possible.
[06:44] Marco Diaz: We support policy-based routing — you can set a SLO-based fallback: when queue latency or CPU > threshold, send overflow to Redwood-hosted model variant. That requires tenant config to allow ephemeral logs to cross account, we document those tradeoffs.
[06:58] Sarah Miller: What's the security tradeoff on that? We can't send PHI to hosted unless it's redacted.
[07:07] Alex Chen: Right, for PHI-sensitive workloads you should keep everything private. For less-sensitive workloads fallback is fine; we can also run a scrubber on the edge or route only metadata to hosted. We'll note options.
[07:22] Lena Ortiz: We'll need a written runbook for the scrubber and a confirmation that fallback logs don't include raw prompts unless allowed.
[07:31] Alex Chen: Noted — action item for Redwood to document.
[07:35] [08:00] Priya Nair: Quick demo of perf chart — (screen share noise) P95 down to ~310ms after kernel patch, throughput up 18% at concurrency 16, but tails at concurrency 64. The chart shows KV hit rate correlated to tail.
[08:20] Jamal Reyes: That matches our runs. If we cap concurrency per instance and scale horizontally can we avoid tails?
[08:30] Marco Diaz: Yes, our autoscaler policy can keep per-instance concurrency below the threshold; you trade a bit of capacity for steadier latency. We'll propose autoscale thresholds.
[08:40] Sarah Miller: Ok, tradeoffs are acceptable.
[08:42] Alex Chen: To recap — Redwood sends network diagram and exact SG/route examples, kernel/flag list, and security doc. Nova runs final bench and confirms peering propagation. Schedule security deep-dive week of 2026-04-03. Target final pilot perf run week of 2026-04-06.
[08:58] Priya Nair: I'll upload the tuning notes and create an eval run ticket.
[09:03] Jamal Reyes: I'll follow up on the peering test and share logs.
[09:07] Lena Ortiz: I'll consolidate compliance questions and share them.
[09:10] Alex Chen: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send notes and next steps.
[09:15] Meeting end.
